CausalChain: miR-495 acts on common targets related to drug transport and EMT regulatory networks -> in NSCLC, its modulation results in reduced expression of resistance genes and reversal of EMT, whereas in SCLC, miR-495 activates the ETK/BMX pathway promoting EMT and chemoresistance -> TGF-β signaling impacts miR-200 family expression via promoter methylation, leading to an intermediate EMT state -> variations in strand-specific miR-125a (3p versus 5p) influence distinct targets (eg, Fyn in pancreatic cancer versus STAT3 in esophageal carcinoma) -> Context-specific factors such as cell type and epigenetic modifications lead to these contradictory outcomes.
Hypothesis: The paradoxical roles of select microRNAs (eg, miR-495 and the miR-200 family) in regulating EMT and drug resistance are not inherent conflicting functions, but rather reflect a context-dependent modulation in which the tumor microenvironment, cell type-specific feedback mechanisms, and strand-specific biogenesis of miRNAs converge to determine their net phenotypic impact. In other words, the same miRNA may exert opposing effects on drug resistance depending on the precise cellular context, including differences in TGF-β pathway activity and the complement of circulating RNA-binding proteins.
Abstract: In the vast and complex field of microRNA‐regulated epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) and its link to stemness and drug resistance, several studies present what may appear as subtle contradictory findings. In our analysis we have identified three such areas of interpretive tension. First, certain microRNAs, such as miR‐495, are reported to reverse cisplatin resistance in non–small cell lung carcinoma cells, yet in other contexts, for example in small cell lung cancer, the same miRNA has been associated with promotion of EMT‐related chemoresistance. Second, the TGF‐β signaling axis – a classical inducer of EMT – is variously shown to be directly targeted by the miR‐200 family (with some studies highlighting its repressive role on several isoforms) while others report that chronic TGF‐β treatment leads to downregulation of the miR‐200 promoter via epigenetic modifications, ultimately producing an intermediate EMT state rather than a full reversal to an epithelial phenotype. Third, investigations of strand‐specific expression products of precursors such as miR‐125 have yielded inconsistent roles in different cancer types, with the 3p or 5p arms seemingly involved in divergent pathways that modulate chemoresistance and tumor cell plasticity, thereby highlighting potential context‐dependent regulatory differences. Our review raises the possibility that these contradictions may be reconciled when considering the tumor type, microenvironmental cues, and the dynamic feedback loops in miRNA–target interactions.
